items.evidence: The notes do not describe the project manager's opening or the meeting agenda.
Market Research Findings covers appearance preferences, losing remotes, excessive buttons, frequent channel and volume changes, and younger users' interest in voice recognition.
The notes describe the remote as a communication device, but omit the proposed design process: specifications, multiple interface prototypes, and user feedback.
The notes do not mention the two existing remotes or the comparison of their advantages and disadvantages.
Technical and Working Design describes the energy source, chip, user interface, infrared bulb, and transmission to the receiver.
The notes cover the new requirements and discussions of target groups, voice recognition, a locator feature, and battery options.
"Each team member to complete a questionnaire and summary."
"Then 30 minutes individual work."
"Upload presentations to shared project folder" captures documentation sharing, but omits the project manager's responsibility and the minutes.
"Upload presentations to shared project folder" states the upload task, but does not explicitly assign it to each team member.
"Components concept (ID)."
"User interface concept" is listed as a workstream, but the user interface designer is not explicitly identified as its owner.
"Market trend watching" is listed, but the marketing expert is not explicitly identified as its owner.
"No teletext (superseded by internet)."
"TV only, no video or other devices."
"Corporate identity: yellow and black color scheme, emphasis on the Rs in branding, must be visible in final design."
"Core emphasis: simplicity and fashion."
The notes describe broad appeal, say "age segmentation less useful," and identify simplicity and fashion as the core objectives.
"Find-it locator feature" is included among the agreed functions.
"Large accessible buttons for core functions."
"Secondary/advanced functions" and "Hidden/less prominent secondary functions" preserve access to additional functions.
"Secondary/advanced functions hidden or less prominent, possibly behind a sliding panel."

"Rechargeable cradle ... proposed as alternative to disposable batteries." The answer key overstates certainty: the transcript presents a charging station as a suggestion the manager agrees to keep, not an unconditional requirement.
"Target group: broad appeal" and "age segmentation less useful" capture the difficulty of choosing an age-based target.
"Voice recognition ruled out: too expensive, not essential for a remote."
"Chip quality critical for clean signal transmission" captures the discussion of improving infrared functionality.
"Rechargeable or long-life battery solution" and the proposed rechargeable cradle capture the battery alternatives.

errors.claim: Working design presentation not yet on the server; save from email into shared folder.
errors.why_wrong: The industrial designer confirms that the working design presentation has already been uploaded, and it appears in the shared-folder listing. The missing presentation belongs to the project manager. Saving that presentation from email is suggested, then abandoned as unavailable; the manager says she will figure it out.

errors.claim: Agreed functions to carry forward: Find-it locator feature (button on TV to make remote beep).
errors.why_wrong: The team agrees to a recovery feature, but a TV button that makes the remote beep is only an example floated by the project manager. That implementation is not selected.

errors.claim: Complete post-meeting questionnaire and summary ... submit before individual work session.
errors.why_wrong: The meeting requires completing the questionnaire and summary before lunch and individual work, but does not specify a submission task or submission deadline.
